To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we compared the relative protein expression levels in five pancreatic cell lines, identified over 8000 unique proteins, and demonstrated that Lys-C/trypsins is a superior protease for proteomics.
we have identified 8000+ proteins across 5 different pancreatic cell lines, and that we have identified the advantages of LYS/C+trypsin over LYS/C-only for proteomics.
we have compared quantitatively the expression levels of thousands proteins across 5 cell lines commonly used by pancreatic cancer researchers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the proteome-wide protein expression profiling across five pancreatic cell lines, using tandem mass tags (10-plex), and the effects of different digestion methods (Lys-C/trypsi vs. Lys-C) on proteomic data sets.

the identification and quantification of proteins in five pancreatic cell lines, which are commonly used as models for pancreatic cancer research, and to determine the effects of two different proteases (lysC/trypsin and lysC) on the proteomic data.
the development and implementation of new methods for the analysis of complex biological samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of Lys-C alone is not sufficient for a complete proteomics analysis.
the proteomes of the 5 cell types are not only distinct from each other but also from the proteomes of other cell types.
Lys-C/trysin digestion of the proteome of pancreatic cancer cell lines results in a higher number of identified proteins and peptides compared to Lys-C only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a resource for the community to study protein expression differences across 5 pancreatic cancer cell lines.
we have generated a proteome-wide protein expression dataset across five cell lines, with a focus on the pancreatic cell lines.
we compared the proteome-wide protein expression levels of five commonly used pancreatic cell lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteomics can be a powerful tool to study pancreatic cells, and the results can be used to design experiments to test hypotheses and to understand the biology of pancreatic cells.
the use of Lys-C and trypsin as opposed to Lys-C alone can increase the depth and quality of discovery proteomics data.
proteomics can now be applied to the study of pancreatic cancer cell lines to provide a more comprehensive view of protein expression.
